html:
Vailima was the estate above Apia where the Scottish writer Robert Louis Stevenson lived from 1890 until his death in 1894. Samoans called him Tusitala, the teller of tales.

Stevenson wrote A Footnote to History about the civil wars and the rivalry of Germany, Britain and the United States. He took the side of Samoan chiefs against the foreign officials, which made him enemies.

When he died, Samoans cut a path up Mount Vaea and carried him to a grave on the summit. Vailima later became the governors' residence under German and New Zealand rule and is now a museum. The Mau remembered him as a friend.
